arxiv-1709-02301.description: Abstract Measurements of longitudinal flow correlations are presented for charged particles in the pseudorapidity range | η | < 2.4 |\eta|<2.4 using 7 μ \mu b -1 and 470 μ \mu b -1 of Pb+Pb collisions at s NN = 2.76 \sqrt{s_{\textrm{NN}}}=2.76 and 5.02 TeV, respectively, recorded by the ATLAS detector at the LHC.

arxiv-2102-11626.title: Fast acquisition of spin-wave dispersion by compressed sensing
arxiv-2102-11626.creator: Ryo Kainuma 1, Keita Matsumoto 1,2, Takuya Satoh 1
arxiv-2102-11626.description: Abstract For the realization of magnonic devices, spin-wave dispersions need to be identified. Recently, the time-resolved pump-probe imaging method combined with the Fourier transform was demonstrated for obtaining the dispersions in the lower-wavenumber regime. However, the measurement takes a long time when the sampling rate is sufficiently high.

arxiv-2209-03610.title: Tunneling of Bell Particles, Page Curve and
arxiv-2209-03610.creator: Black Hole Information
arxiv-2209-03610.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Black Hole Information. We propose that the quantum states of black hole responsible for the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy are given by a thin shell of Bell particles located at the region just underneath the horizon. We argue that the configuration can be stabilized by a new kind of degeneracy pressure which is suggested by a noncommutative geometry in the interior of the black hole. Black hole singularity is avoided.

arxiv-2405-09548.title: Efficient Bilevel Source Mask Optimization
arxiv-2405-09548.creator: Guojin Chen, Hongquan He, Peng Xu, Hao Geng, Bei Yu
arxiv-2405-09548.description: Abstract . Resolution Enhancement Techniques (RETs) are critical to meet the demands of advanced technology nodes. Among RETs, Source Mask Optimization (SMO) is pivotal, concurrently optimizing both the source and the mask to expand the process window. Traditional SMO methods, however, are limited by sequential and alternating optimizations, leading to extended runtimes without performance guarantees.

arxiv-2411-04863.title: OneProt: Towards Multi-Modal Protein Foundation Models
arxiv-2411-04863.creator: Klemens Flöge, Srisruthi Udayakumar, Johanna Sommer, Marie Piraud, Stefan Kesselheim, Vincent Fortuin, Stephan Günnemann, Karel J van der Weg, Holger Gohlke, Erinc Merdivan, Alina Bazarova

Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence have enabled multi-modal systems to model and translate diverse information spaces. Extending beyond text and vision, we introduce OneProt, a multi-modal AI for proteins that integrates structural, sequence, text, and binding site data.

arxiv-2511-11749.description: Abstract This research paper investigates how machine learning-driven data replication strategies can enhance fault tolerance in large-scale distributed systems. Traditional replication methods, which rely on static configurations, often struggle to adapt to dynamic workloads and unexpected failures, leading to inefficient resource utilization and prolonged downtime. pmc-10666939.creator: Nikol Mayo-Puchoc, Jenny Bejarano-Carranza, Rubí Paredes-Angeles, Ana Lucía Vilela-Estrada, Jackeline García-Serna, Noelia Cusihuaman-Lope, David Villarreal-Zegarra, Victoria Cavero, Sara Ardila-Gómez
pmc-10666939.description: Governments globally deployed various non-pharmacological public health measures to respond to the COVID-19 pandemic (i.e. lockdowns and suspension of transportation, amongst others); some of these measures had an influence on society’s mental health. Specific mental health policies were therefore implemented to mitigate the potential mental health impact of the pandemic.

pmc-10669611.title: Investigation on the Energy-Absorbing Properties of Bionic Spider Web Structure
pmc-10669611.creator: Baocheng Xie, Xilong Wu, Xuhui Ji, Marc Weissburg
pmc-10669611.description: In recent years, spider webs have received significant attention due to their exceptional mechanical properties, including strength, toughness, elasticity, and robustness. Among these spider webs, the orb web is a prevalent type. An orb web’s main framework consists of radial and spiral threads, with elastic and sticky threads used to capture prey.

pmc-11454681.title: 6847 Poorly Differentiated Thyroid Cancer: A Rare Entity
pmc-11454681.creator: Sanna Fatima, Samuel Ward, Amber Champion
pmc-11454681.description: Disclosure: S. Fatima: None. S. Ward: None. A. Champion: None. Introduction: Poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma (PDTC) is a rare thyroid carcinoma originating from follicular epithelial cells. Regarding the degree of differentiation, PDTC ranks between differentiated thyroid cancer and anaplastic thyroid cancer. We hereby present a rare case of PDTC.

pmc-11689403.title: WELL-BEING AND SERVICE USE AMONG VETERANS’ CAREGIVER-SURVIVORS
pmc-11689403.creator: Erin Bouldin, Richard Munoz, Ranak Trivedi, Luci Leykum, Jared Hansen, Stuti Dang
pmc-11689403.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Transitioning from the role of caregiver to survivor following the death of the care recipient can be difficult. Our goal was to describe well-being and bereavement-related service use among family caregivers of Veterans who had recently died. During June-November, 2023, we sent surveys to caregivers of 1,468 Veterans who had participated in a previous survey and whose Veterans had died 3-18 months prior to this survey; 296 (20.1%) caregiver-survivors completed the survey.

pmc-12305087.title: Challenges and solutions in managing dental problems in children with autism
pmc-12305087.creator: Mohammed Al-Beltagi, Abdulrahman Abdullah Al Zahrani, Babu Sandilyan Mani, Ehab Mohamed Hantash, Nermin Kamal Saeed, Adel Salah Bediwy, Reem Elbeltagi
pmc-12305087.description: BACKGROUNDChildren with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) face unique challenges in maintaining oral health due to sensory sensitivities, communication difficulties, and behavioral barriers. These factors, along with limited access to ASD-trained dental professionals, increase their risk of dental caries, periodontal disease, bruxism, and other oral health issues. Despite growing awareness of these challenges, a comprehensive synthesis of evidence-based solutions remains lacking.

pmc-12635195.title: MET (c-Met) protein overexpression is an emerging protein biomarker in non-small cell lung cancer
pmc-12635195.creator: Ming-Sound Tsao, Lynette Sholl, Michelle Shiller, Peter Illei, Ignacio I Wistuba, Mary Beth Beasley, Kurt A Schalper, Archana Simmons, Peter Ansell, Sue Beruti, Mari Mino-Kenudson
pmc-12635195.description: MET protein (also known as c-Met protein) overexpression (OE) is an emerging clinically relevant biomarker that is targetable with antibody-drug conjugates. c-Met protein’s prevalence varies, depending on the different OE thresholds, antibodies, and detection methodologies used. Unlike MET genomic aberrations, MET protein OE is a protein biomarker requiring immunohistochemistry (IHC)-based testing.
